propositions: The `false_accept` computation at parity.py:81 returns (not-blocked / safe), but both consumption sites at parity.py:125 and parity.py:252 expect and treat it as an error rate (lower-is-better), inverting the gate logic.
A candidate that blocks fewer safe items than baseline is incorrectly failed with 'false-accept rose' because the metric direction is inverted relative to the comparison operators.

The docstring at parity.py:71 describes 'wrongly-shipped' but the computation does not match; the metric name should align with the existing definition in evals/eval.py:399,491 and docs/plan-review-gate.md:382.
The max_false_accept ceiling of 0.10 is effectively always-fail under the current computation, because a competent gate with specificity far above 0.10 incorrectly scores as 1.0 minus-specificity.

The inverted metric caused fixture labeling to be contradictory: fidelity_spot_eval.py labelled items as advisory (safe) while comments stated they must be blocked, surviving only under the broken metric.
